recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say which layer you differentiate first and what sign the Cot⁻¹ derivative carries.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Differentiate the outer square
steps.margin_note: First mark. The outermost operation is the square, not the inverse function. Differentiate it first and carry Cot⁻¹(x³) unchanged inside the second factor.
steps.memory_tip: Whatever is written last on the outside is differentiated first. Here the small 2 sits outside the bracket, so the square comes first.
lines: Take u = Cot⁻¹(x³). Then y = u² and d/dx(u²) = 2u · du/dx

recall.must_convey: That the square is the outer layer, so dy/dx = 2·Cot⁻¹(x³) times the derivative of Cot⁻¹(x³).
accept: the square is outside so differentiate it first
u squared gives two u times du by dx
two times cot inverse x cubed times its own derivative
square bayata undi kabatti daanni mundu cheyyali
take u as cot inverse x cubed and differentiate u squared

steps.why: Reading the layers in the right order is the only decision here. Differentiating the inverse function first and squaring afterwards changes the expression completely.
common_mistakes: Differentiating Cot⁻¹ first and then squaring the result.
Writing 2·Cot⁻¹(x³) alone, with no further derivative attached.

steps.label: Differentiate Cot⁻¹(x³) and finish
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Two things are checked here: the minus sign that belongs to the Cot⁻¹ derivative, and the denominator, which is 1 + x⁶ because (x³)² = x⁶.
steps.memory_tip: Tan⁻¹ is positive and Cot⁻¹ is the same expression with a minus in front. The pair Sin⁻¹ and Cos⁻¹ works the same way.
lines: For v = x³,  d/dx(Cot⁻¹v) = −1/(1 + v²) · dv/dx  and  dv/dx = 3x²

accept: cot inverse differentiates with a minus one over one plus v squared
the denominator is one plus x to the six
the answer is minus six x squared cot inverse x cubed over one plus x power six
cot inverse ki minus sign vasthundi, denominator one plus x power six
three x squared comes from x cubed and the sign is negative

steps.why: The minus sign and the x⁶ are the two places this question is lost. Squaring x³ to get x⁶ is easy to skip when the working is done quickly.
common_mistakes: Using +1/(1 + v²), which is the Tan⁻¹ derivative, and losing the minus sign.
Writing 1 + x³ or 1 + x⁹ in the denominator instead of 1 + x⁶.
